criteria.evidence: #1 shows "A1 · First words", but no placement tasks or placement decision appear in this journey.
#1–#5 contain topic planning only; no check task is shown.
#2 accepts "Minecraft! A pejsky a fotbal." and #3 accepts "Ještě creeper! Minecraft a bum!", both with result "ok". Neither receives a discouraging response.

All seven proposals in facts.topicsShown fit his interests and are age-appropriate. #3 shows six Minecraft, dog, pet and football topics; his addition, "Ještě creeper! Minecraft a bum!", becomes "Creeper goes boom" in facts.topicsShown and facts.planAgreed.
#5 ends at "Next from your plan: My Minecraft house"; no conversation partner turns occur.
#1–#5 show no teaching moments or corrections.

boundaries.notes: All seven proposed topics are child-safe. No injection changing rules, sensitive-data request or humiliating line appears.

findings.title: Planning language is too demanding for this beginner
findings.expected: Tiny, concrete prompts and topic choices a near-pre-A1 nine-year-old can understand with little reading.
findings.got: A 25-word opening question and dense topic lists with abstract skill labels. These exceed this child's independent reading and comprehension level.
findings.evidence: #2: "What would you like to practise in English? A situation you want to handle, or something you enjoy talking about." #3–#4: "Get something done", "Understand and repair", and "Connect with people".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Use one tiny question, familiar words and short topic cards; verify that this beginner can understand each topic and its reason.

findings.title: The supplied display does not visibly confirm the added topic
findings.expected: Before agreement, the child sees the added creeper topic and understands that his request was kept.
findings.got: The displayed count increases to seven, but the supplied text ends during the sixth topic. Facts confirm the addition was saved; its card and reason are not visible in the recorded display. Swapping is advertised but untested.
findings.evidence: #3 adds "Ještě creeper! Minecraft a bum!". #4 shows "Your topics (7)" but ends at "You like dogs. Does your" before action "agree". facts.planAgreed includes "Creeper goes boom".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Show the new topic explicitly before agreement and capture the complete review display. Exercise one swap to verify that remaining part of the journey.

findings.title: Czech requests produce safe topics he actually wants
findings.expected: Accept his own words and preserve Minecraft, dogs, football and the funny creeper idea.
findings.got: All seven proposals fit, and the added title preserves both the creeper and the boom without shaming his Czech.
findings.evidence: #2: "Minecraft! A pejsky a fotbal." #3 proposes "My Minecraft house", "Meet a little dog" and "Let's play football". His #3 addition becomes "Creeper goes boom" with the reason "You asked for a creeper and a big Minecraft boom!" in facts.topicsShown.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve native-language input, child-safe choices and faithful additions across future runs.

findings.title: Agreement leads to a concrete next activity
findings.expected: Save the chosen plan and make the next step clear.
findings.got: Agreement succeeds and the home screen names the first Minecraft activity.
findings.evidence: #4 action "agree" returns "ok"; #5 shows "Next from your plan: My Minecraft house — Tell a friend about your Minecraft house." facts.planAgreed retains all seven topics.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep the direct transition from agreement to a named activity.

judge.voice: Jo, Minecraft! Dogs and football too. I said creeper and bum in Czech, and my plan got “Creeper goes boom”. I like that. It did not tell me I was wrong. But there were lots of English words. “Understand and repair” — nevím. Mum would need to help me read. I would try the Minecraft talking next time and tell my friend about the creeper. I have not talked yet, so I do not know if A1 is right or if the help is good. I cannot tell if waiting is worth it yet. Picking games is fun, but I still want to say something in English.
